processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 1970-01-01..1970-12-31. The WHO Global Health Observatory annual series (indicator CHOLERA_0000000001) likewise has no COG record before 1978. Evidence type: Documented_Absence from WHO first-infection statement. Surveillance system status during absence: partial - WHO tracked newly infected countries globally under the International Health Regulations, but national-level surveillance capacity in Congo in the 1970s is not independently documented.

source: UN OCHA Humanitarian Situation Report Republic of Congo April-May 1998
processing_notes: Source states: 'HEALTH AND NUTRITION 7. As of 6 May, a total of 3,236 cholera cases were reported in the Kouilou region of southern Congo, mainly in the economic hub of Pointe-Noire, and 104 deaths have been attributed to the disease. Between 20 and 30 new cases were being reported every day, but the number of deaths from the disease has dropped drastically since February.' - interpreted as 1436 sCh cases, 19 deaths. INCIDENT count for 16 March - 6 May 1998, derived from OCHA's cumulative figure of 3,236 cases / 104 deaths at 6 May minus the 1,800 cases / 85 deaths already documented to mid-March 1998 in this file (Index 57: 1997-11-27..1998-02-05 = 485 cases/83 deaths; Index 58: 1998-02-06..02-26 = 783/2; Index 60: 1998-02-27..03-15 = 532/0; sum 1,800 cases and 85 deaths). Those three rows are independently corroborated by the same OCHA series: the Jan-Feb 1998 report states the outbreak was 'affecting 1,268 people up to 26 February, with some 85 deaths' (= 485+783 cases and 83+2 deaths exactly) and the March 1998 report states 'Over 1,800 cases of cholera have been reported in Pointe-Noire up to around mid-March'. GEOGRAPHY: OCHA attributes the 3,236 to 'the Kouilou region of southern Congo, mainly in the economic hub of Pointe-Noire'. In 1998 Pointe-Noire was administratively part of Kouilou region; it became a separate department only in 2004. The row is placed at AFR::COG::Pointe-Noire because the source names Pointe-Noire as where the cases mainly were and because the whole preceding series for this epidemic is already recorded there. The alternative reading - that some of these cases belong to rural Kouilou - is not quantifiable: WHO Disease Outbreak News of 10 February 1998 says of the rural Kouilou localities Madingo-Kayes and Kaka Mueka that 'Complete figures are not available', and that is recorded in ./data/COG/cholera_presence_ai.csv as presence-without-count. processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 2002-01-01..2005-12-31. Source states: 'Le cholera. Apres les epidemies de cholera observees en 1998, 1999 et 2001 a Brazzaville et a Pointe-Noire, aucun cas n'a ete notifie sur l'ensemble du territoire de 2001 a 2005.'. Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: operational. REPLACES retracted Index 1 (2000-2006), which wrongly asserted absence over 2000 (9 cases), 2001 (Brazzaville/Pointe-Noire epidemics named by this same source) and 2006 (175 cases). Window deliberately starts 2002-01-01, not 2001-01-01, because the same sentence names 2001 as an epidemic year; the 'de 2001 a 2005' phrasing is read as 'from the end of the 2001 epidemic to 2005'. Surveillance status OPERATIONAL: this is a positive WHO country-office assertion that nothing was notified nationwide, not an inference from missing tables, and Congo demonstrably notified cases to WHO in 1997-2000 and again from 2006. CORROBORATION: WHO GHO indicator CHOLERA_0000000001 carries an EXPLICIT 0 for COG in 2005 (one of only 20 explicit country zeros in the whole 2005 series), i.e. Congo filed a nil annual return for 2005; WER annual Africa tables for 2002, 2003 and 2004 do not list Congo; data/COG/cholera_data_jhu.csv Index 4901 independently carries 2005 = 0 cases / 0 deaths. REGIONAL CROSS-CHECK: this is absence during a regionally ACTIVE period - DRC reported 31 618 cases in 2002, 27 272 in 2003 and 7 665 in 2004 - so the claim rests on the explicit WHO country-office statement rather than on quiet neighbours. Confidence held at 0.85 rather than 0.9 for that reason.

EVIDENCE GRADE DELIBERATELY LOW (Inferred_Absence, 0.6). This is absence inferred from omission, and omission is demonstrably unreliable for this country: the WHO Country Cooperation Strategy Congo 2009-2013 documents cholera epidemics at Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire in 2001 that appear in neither the WER 2001 table nor the GHO series. REGIONAL CROSS-CHECK: 2010 was a major Central African cholera year - both land neighbours that report to WHO in volume, DRC (13 884 cases) and Cameroon (10 759 cases, CFR 6.1%), were in large epidemics, and Congo's own next epidemic began on the Congo/Oubangui river corridor in June 2011 spreading from DRC (WHO DON 22 July 2011). Absence here is absence under regional pressure, which the protocol says demands a stronger source than exists. Surveillance PARTIAL: no independent evidence located that cholera surveillance was actively excluding cases in Congo during 2010.

Surveillance system status during absence: operational. Closes the interval between the AI absence block ending 2024-12-31 (Index 12) and the onset of the 2025-2026 epidemic. The Ministry of Health's own epidemic curve places the INDEX CASE on 21 June 2025, so no cholera case was notified anywhere in the country from 1 January to 20 June 2025. CORROBORATION: the WHO cholera surveillance dashboard weekly series in data/COG/cholera_data_who.csv carries no cases for every week from 2024-12-30 to 2025-06-15 and its first positive week is 2025-06-16..2025-06-22 with 1 case, exactly consistent with a 21 June index case. Surveillance OPERATIONAL: the index case was detected and notified through routine surveillance, the national incident management system (SGI) was activated on 26 July 2025, and the same MoH/WHO SITREP series reports concurrent shigellosis and typhoid surveillance. Evidence graded Documented_Absence because this is a positive dated statement of epidemic onset from the national authority, not an absence of search results; confidence held at 0.85 rather than 0.9 because an index-case date bounds detected transmission rather than directly certifying nationwide zero reporting week by week.
